rationale: Both Section 7.2 (unqualified non-infringement warranty) and Section 13.1 (IP infringement indemnity excluding misuse, modification/combination, and third-party materials, and disclaiming "other liability") govern third-party IP infringement while Section 12.2 carves out both indemnification obligations and IP infringement from the liability cap, inviting inconsistency as to whether Section 7.2 gives an independent uncapped warranty claim bypassing Section 13.1's exclusions.

rationale: Section 11.1 conditions automatic five-year renewal on Reseller having "achieved the Annual Milestones," which depends entirely on Section 2.1's unagreed future "Annual Milestones" and leaves unclear how a sub-50% shortfall cured under Section 2.2(b) or a conversion to non-exclusivity under Section 2.2(a) affects automatic renewal.

rationale: Section 10.6 causes the confidentiality and healthcare privacy duties in Sections 10.1 and 10.2 to survive expiration or termination indefinitely, while Section 10.5 governs injunctive enforcement of those duties without bond.

rationale: Clause B broadly excuses either party from liability for "any delay in performance or non-performance" caused by force majeure (including "failure of ... telecommunications, data systems or networks") without excluding payment obligations, leaving unclear whether a force majeure payment delay suspends Clause A's automatic cross-acceleration of "all sums owing" and statutory late-payment interest.

rationale: Clause A states that "the price of Product shall be Seller's price therefor as of the date of shipment" and allows Seller to "change any price ... upon no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice" ("Except as otherwise provided"), whereas Clause B sets a 2020 grade-based pricing schedule without stating whether it overrides or remains subject to Clause A's unilateral price-change mechanism.

rationale: Clause B's Section 6(c) makes Company's rights in the Product and marketing collateral expressly "Subject to ... in particular 5 above," meaning Company's commercialization and resulting royalty revenues under Clause A's Section 4 depend on Talent's prior approval under Section 5, which currently lacks any reasonableness standard or response deadline.

rationale: Clause B's conditional one-year exclusive appointment of Distributor in "[*]" operates directly through Clause A's amendment expanding the Territory to "the United States and [*]," while leaving unstated whether exclusivity rules for the United States under the original Agreement remain unaffected during and after the initial period.

rationale: Section 4(b) allows Client to 'cancel' upon failure to agree on Year 2 WebCrawler performance details without clarifying whether cancellation terminates only Section 4 or the entire Agreement including Section 2's Excite Lifestyle Channel sponsorship, and both clauses rely on uncertain good-faith negotiation for Year 2 deliverables.

rationale: Sections 3(D) and 4 both govern fee retention upon termination 'for any reason' using inconsistent terms ('royalties' vs. Endorsement 'fee' and mutual-agreement License 'fees'), while Section 3(A) ends all further responsibility on 60-day termination 'except as provided in Section 5' without carving out Section 4.

rationale: Section 8 specifies no post-termination survival duration for trade secrets in 8(A)-(B) and limits PCQ's non-disclosure of ABW's use to 'during the initial term' in 8(C), so its post-termination enforceability depends on Section 12(B)'s open-ended survival of confidentiality 'unless specifically stated otherwise'.

rationale: Section 10 prohibits assignment only by ABW without PCQ's consent, leaving unclear whether PCQ may freely assign the Agreement to a third party despite PCQ's strict obligations under Sections 8(B)-(C) to safeguard ABW's proprietary information and not disclose the Agreement's existence to other parties.

rationale: Clause A(C) requires PCQ to indemnify ABW for 'any and all claims, liabilities, or obligations' resulting from PCQ's negligence or non-performance of its covenants, whereas Section 6(A)-(B) disclaims all liability for data errors and for 'delays or interruptions... from whatever cause' without carving out Section 9 indemnification.

rationale: Clause B ('If elected pursuant to the Agreement') supplies the hourly rate for the 'Termination Assistance Services' defined in Clause A ('at additional cost to Client' and 'Fee billable assistance'), while Clause B depends on Clause A for the election trigger, 3-month scope, and term-extension rule, with a slight term-name mismatch and bracketed rate ($[125.00 per hour]).

rationale: Clause B defines 'Fees' solely as fees 'for Project Services and Deliverables as Described in the SOW' payable per the 'Fee Payment Schedule' in an SOW, leaving unclear whether Clause A's hourly rate ($[125.00 per hour]) for Client Termination Assistance Services is governed by Section 5's payment schedule, wire instructions, and material-breach rules or when those hourly charges become due.

rationale: HSWI's right in Clause B to translate Affinities ('Where rights permit') depends directly on the third-party materials World Book chooses to incorporate when creating those Affinities under Clause A, which does not obligate World Book to clear or identify missing translation rights upon delivery.

rationale: Clause B operates on the 'Updating Services' defined in Clause A (Section 1.28) and ties all updates provided under Updating Services (even when translated into Chinese) back to 'the license herein for that Content which is being updated' in Clause A (Section 2.1), while carving out HSWI's right to update Content to correct errors notwithstanding Section 2.1(iv).

rationale: Calculating the start of Clause A's 'thirty (30) days prior written notice' for termination relies on Clause B's notice rule, under which mailed notice is deemed given 'when actually received or within fourteen (14) days of mailing... whichever first occurs', making the deemed-delivery date uncertain anywhere within that 14-day window.

rationale: Clause A keeps an assigning Party bound by 'the continuing obligations of confidentiality and nonuse applicable to such Party prior to the assignment', which directly incorporates and extends Clause B's 20-year confidentiality and Program-only use restrictions on Background Information after assignment.

rationale: Clause A explicitly lists 'Article 4 (Disclosure, Confidentiality and Restricted Use)' and 'Article 7 (License to Program Results)' as surviving termination, ensuring Clause B's 20-year confidentiality and Article 7-linked use restrictions for Program Information continue post-termination.

rationale: Clause A disclaims any promise or intention 'to enter into any other agreement of any nature' while carving out only a good-faith negotiation for Generation 2 Technology demonstration, directly conflicting with Clause B's separate commitment requiring FCE to negotiate a royalty-bearing Power Applications license agreement if it decides not to pursue Power Applications.

rationale: Section 7 expressly preserves and triggers the Company and Bank's joint and several reimbursement obligation "Whether or not ... the Conversion is terminated" and when "unable to sell the minimum number of shares", directly operating upon the Agent's termination triggers in Section 12(a)-(b) without excluding termination caused by Agent default.

rationale: Clause 1.12 deems legal terms for any jurisdiction other than Australia to approximate the corresponding 'Australian legal term', creating interpretive uncertainty alongside Clause 24.1 which requires the agreement to be construed in accordance with 'Ohio law'.

rationale: Clause 7.2 permits XFN to renew for 'an additional term of ten (10) years' at the expiry of the Term, while Clause 8.1 allows XFN to terminate 'this Agreement' on 30 days' notice without clarifying whether Clause 8.1 applies during the renewed term or how early termination affects the renewal option.

rationale: Section 11.1(b) requires Client upon termination for any reason to pay Fees for 'all Services and Deliverables provided by Developer to Client up to and including the date of termination', leaving unclear whether Deliverables delivered before completion of 'Client testing' under Section 3.1's Milestones trigger payment.

rationale: Section 3(a)'s obligation for MMMW to provide on-call service "during the term of this Agreement" depends on Sections 1(c)–(e) and 2(a) for when the Initial Term begins ("Effective Date") and when support coverage is suspended and becomes billable between the "Effective Date" and receipt of a late renewal agreement.

rationale: Section 10.03 ('When this Agreement expires or terminates, the following provisions shall remain in effect') operates directly on Section 10.01's termination trigger (later of the third anniversary or ETI ceasing to be an NTL Subsidiary), while Section 10.01 relies on its general 'Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement' proviso to preserve survival of Articles II, VI, VIII, XI, XII and ancillary licenses under Section 10.03.

rationale: Section 6.06 bars the Grantee from granting third-party sublicenses 'except as expressly provide[d] in Section 6.03', making the scope of permitted third-party pass-through rights dependent on Section 6.03's end-user licensing ('to license the use of Licensed Products') and conditional 'have made' manufacturing rights even though Section 6.03 does not use the term 'sublicenses'.

rationale: Section 6.02's 'irrevocable... worldwide license' under Entrust Patents is granted 'Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement' and 'to the extent of its legal right to do so', making it dependent on and narrowed by Section 6.07(a)'s carve-out permitting Grantor to enter future third-party-funded development contracts that exclude resulting Patents without breach.
